concepts.def: Jobs: médico/médica (doctor), profesor/profesora, ingeniero/ingeniera, abogado/abogada (lawyer), enfermero/enfermera (nurse).
Simple future for plans: 'Trabajaré...' (I will work). Add endings to infinitive: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án.
'Me gustaría ser...' (I would like to be...), 'Quisiera estudiar...' (I would like to study...).
University vocab: la universidad, hacer una carrera (do a degree), las prácticas (work experience).
Workplace: el sueldo (salary), el jefe (boss), una entrevista (interview), un contrato.
Justifying choices: 'porque soy creativo/responsable/trabajador'. Useful for personal statements.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area D: The World of Work — a core area of GCSE Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area D: The World of Work brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area D: The World of Work.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which sentence means 'I would like to be a doctor'?
options: Me gustaría ser médico.
Me gusta ser médico.
Me gustaría siendo médico.
Soy ser médico.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I don't see anything' in Spanish?
options: Christmas y Easter.
No veo nada (double negative is correct).
Veo nada.
No veo algo.

mcqs.q: How do you write 'Christmas' and 'Easter' in Spanish?
options: Navidád y Pascua (incorrect accent).
It means 'a brother' (indefinite).

Navidad y Pascua (note: Semana Santa for Holy Week traditions).
